title: How Meta Ads Actually Work
subtitle: The ad auction explained in plain English
youtube_title: How Meta Ads Actually Work: The Ad Auction Explained | Meta Ads Course Lesson 1
description: Lesson 1 of the free Meta Ads course. Before you spend a single dollar on Facebook or Instagram ads, you need to understand how Meta decides which ad to show. In this lesson: the ad auction, the three factors that decide the winner (bid, estimated action rate, ad quality), why the Boost button wastes money, and what this means for your campaigns.

slides.narration: Hi, I'm Khalil Baghirov, and welcome to lesson one of this free Meta Ads course. Before you spend a single dollar on Facebook or Instagram ads, you need to understand one thing: how Meta actually decides which ad to show, to whom, and at what price. Get this right, and every lesson after this will make sense.

slides.text: Every ad you see *won an auction*
slides.narration: Here's the core idea. Every single ad you see on Facebook or Instagram won an auction. Each time someone opens the app, Meta has a few empty ad slots and thousands of advertisers who want them. In a fraction of a second, an auction runs, and one ad wins.

slides.title: Three things decide the winner
items: Your bid: what you are willing to pay
Estimated action rate: how likely this person is to act
Ad quality: how people react to your ad
slides.narration: Three things decide who wins. First, your bid, which is what you are willing to pay for the result you want. Second, the estimated action rate, which is Meta's prediction of how likely this specific person is to click, message, or buy. And third, ad quality, which is based on how people react to your ad: do they engage, hide it, or report it?

slides.title: Meta's auction formula
slides.formula: Total value = Bid × Estimated action rate + Ad quality
slides.note: The highest *total value* wins, not the highest bid
slides.narration: Meta combines these into one number called total value. Total value equals your bid, multiplied by the estimated action rate, plus ad quality. The ad with the highest total value wins. Notice what this means: the highest bid does not automatically win. A smaller advertiser with a relevant, high quality ad can beat a big brand with a boring one, and pay less.

slides.title: Boost button vs Ads Manager
slides.narration: This is also why the Boost button often wastes money. Boosting a post usually tells Meta to find people who will like or view it. So Meta happily delivers likes. In Ads Manager, you choose the real objective, like leads or sales, and Meta uses its prediction models to find people who are likely to take that action.

slides.title: What happens after you click publish
items: Meta tests your ad on different people
slides.narration: So what happens after you publish a campaign? You choose an objective. Meta starts showing your ad to different people and watches who responds. This is called the learning phase. As data comes in, the system gets better at predicting who will act, and your results usually become more stable and cheaper.

slides.title: What this means for you
items: Pick the objective that matches your real goal
Make ads that people actually want to engage with
Give the system enough budget and data
Don't edit your campaign every day
slides.narration: Here is what this means for you in practice. One: pick the objective that matches your real business goal. Two: make ads people actually want to engage with, because quality lowers your cost. Three: give the system enough budget and data to learn. And four: don't edit your campaign every day, because big changes can restart the learning phase.

slides.title: Your homework
items: Open Ads Manager and look at the objective list
Write down the one result your business needs most
Match it to an objective before lesson 2
slides.narration: Your homework for today. Open Ads Manager and look at the list of campaign objectives. Write down the one result your business needs most: messages, leads, or sales. Then match it to an objective. We will use it in the next lessons.

slides.next: Setting Up Business Manager the Right Way
slides.narration: In the next lesson, we will set up Business Manager the right way, so your ad account is safe and ready to scale. Subscribe so you don't miss it, and I'll see you in lesson two.
